# SerDes and SerDe properties

The SerDe (SerializationLibrary) of a Hive table decides how its files are read and written. A table property overrides the SerDe property of the same name and keys are case-sensitive, as in Hive. Properties not listed here are ignored. Partitions are read with the table's SerDe properties.

| SerDe | Matched by | Files | Read with | Written | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ParquetHiveSerDe (`org.apache.hadoop.hive.ql.io.parquet.serde.ParquetHiveSerDe`) | `parquet` | parquet | read_parquet (columns by name) | yes |  |
| LazySimpleSerDe (`org.apache.hadoop.hive.serde2.lazy.LazySimpleSerDe`) | `lazysimpleserde` | csv | read_csv (columns by position, fields as text, then cast) | yes | Fields are not quoted. A value that does not parse as its column type is NULL. Writes refuse values that hold the delimiter or a line break, or equal the NULL string. Nested columns (array, map, struct) are refused; a null string holding the delimiter is refused; writes need a single-byte delimiter. |
| OpenCSVSerde (`org.apache.hadoop.hive.serde2.OpenCSVSerde`) | `opencsvserde` | csv | read_csv (columns by position, fields as text, then cast) | yes | There is no NULL: an empty field is an empty string. A boolean field is true when it is 'true' in any case and false otherwise. Writes quote every value and refuse values that hold a line break. Nested columns (array, map, struct) are refused; a quote or escape character of more than one byte is refused; writes need a single-byte delimiter. |
| OpenX JSON (`org.openx.data.jsonserde.JsonSerDe`) | `openx` | json | read_json (one object per line, keys by name) | no: DuckDB writes JSON tables only with the Hive JsonSerDe (org.apache.hive.hcatalog.data.JsonSerDe) | Keys are matched to the columns exactly; the SerDe matches them ignoring case by default. |
| Hive JsonSerDe (`org.apache.hive.hcatalog.data.JsonSerDe`) | `json` | json | read_json (one object per line, keys by name) | yes | Also Hive 3's org.apache.hadoop.hive.serde2.JsonSerDe and any other SerDe whose name holds 'json'. |
| AvroSerDe (`org.apache.hadoop.hive.serde2.avro.AvroSerDe`) | `avro` | avro | read_avro from the avro extension (columns by name) | yes |  |
| OrcSerde | `orcserde` | - | not supported: ORC files, for which this extension has no reader | no | |
| RegexSerDe | `regexserde` | - | not supported: lines parsed with a regular expression | no | |
| MultiDelimitSerDe | `multidelimitserde` | - | not supported: multi-character field delimiters | no | |
| ColumnarSerDe / LazyBinaryColumnarSerDe | `columnarserde` | - | not supported: RCFile files | no | |
| LazyBinarySerDe | `lazybinaryserde` | - | not supported: binary SequenceFile records | no | |

Any other SerDe is not supported. A table of an unsupported SerDe can be inspected with `glue_get_table_response()`.

## Properties

Read and Write say what the property does: the reader / writer option it sets (with the conversion of its value), `ignored` (harmless), `not applied, logged` (the read succeeds and a warning is logged, `CALL enable_logging(level := 'warning')`) or `refused` (the query fails).

| SerDe | Property | Default | Read | Write | CREATE TABLE option | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LazySimpleSerDe | `field.delim` | `\001` | delimiter (byte_code) | delimiter (byte_code) | delimiter | NUL, line breaks and non-ASCII bytes are refused. |
| LazySimpleSerDe | `serialization.format` | `\001` | delimiter (byte_code) | delimiter (byte_code) | delimiter | The delimiter when field.delim is not set. |
| LazySimpleSerDe | `serialization.null.format` | `\N` | null_string (text) | null_string (text) |  |  |
| LazySimpleSerDe | `skip.header.line.count` | `0` | header_lines (count) | header_lines (count); refused when above 1 |  | Also read from the table parameters (TBLPROPERTIES). |
| OpenCSVSerde | `skip.header.line.count` | `0` | header_lines (count) | header_lines (count); refused when above 1 |  | Also read from the table parameters (TBLPROPERTIES). |
| Hive JsonSerDe | `skip.header.line.count` |  | refused when above 0 | refused when above 0 |  |  |
| OpenX JSON | `skip.header.line.count` |  | refused when above 0 | table not written |  |  |
| LazySimpleSerDe | `skip.footer.line.count` |  | refused when above 0 | refused when above 0 |  | Refused rather than returning the footer lines as rows. |
| OpenCSVSerde | `skip.footer.line.count` |  | refused when above 0 | refused when above 0 |  | Refused rather than returning the footer lines as rows. |
| Hive JsonSerDe | `skip.footer.line.count` |  | refused when above 0 | refused when above 0 |  | Refused rather than returning the footer lines as rows. |
| OpenX JSON | `skip.footer.line.count` |  | refused when above 0 | table not written |  | Refused rather than returning the footer lines as rows. |
| LazySimpleSerDe | `escape.delim` |  | refused when set | refused when set |  | DuckDB's reader has no LazySimpleSerDe escaping. |
| LazySimpleSerDe | `serialization.encoding` | `UTF-8` | refused when not UTF-8 | refused when not UTF-8 |  |  |
| LazySimpleSerDe | `serialization.last.column.takes.rest` | `false` | refused when 'true' | refused when 'true' |  |  |
| LazySimpleSerDe | `timestamp.formats` |  | not applied, logged when not empty | ignored |  | Not applied: timestamps are read with DuckDB's default format; a warning is logged. |
| LazySimpleSerDe | `collection.delim` | `\002` | ignored | ignored |  | Harmless: nested columns, the only ones it separates, are refused. |
| OpenCSVSerde | `separatorChar` | `,` | delimiter (character) | delimiter (character) | delimiter |  |
| OpenCSVSerde | `quoteChar` | `"` | quote (character) | quote (character) | quote | A character of more than one byte is refused. |
| OpenCSVSerde | `escapeChar` | `the quote character` | escape (character) | escape (character) | escape | Defaults to the quote character, which reads the doubled quotes Hive writes. A character of more than one byte is refused. |
| OpenCSVSerde | `use.null.for.invalid.data` | `false` | null_for_invalid_data (boolean) | ignored |  | Without it a value that does not parse as its column type fails the query. |
| OpenCSVSerde | `serialization.format` |  | ignored | ignored |  | Harmless: these SerDes do not read it. |
| ParquetHiveSerDe | `serialization.format` |  | ignored | ignored |  | Harmless: these SerDes do not read it. |
| OpenX JSON | `ignore.malformed.json` | `false` | ignore_errors (boolean) | table not written |  | A line that is not valid JSON is a row of NULLs, and a value that does not fit its column NULL (either property enables both). |
| OpenX JSON | `use.null.for.invalid.data` | `false` | ignore_errors (boolean) | table not written |  |  |
| OpenX JSON | `case.insensitive` | `true` | not applied, logged when 'true' | table not written |  | Not applied: keys are matched exactly; a warning is logged when it is true. |
| OpenX JSON | `mapping.*` |  | not applied, logged when not empty | table not written |  | mapping.<column> = <key>: not applied, a warning is logged. |
| OpenX JSON | `dots.in.keys` | `false` | not applied, logged when 'true' | table not written |  | Not applied: a warning is logged when it is true. |
| Hive JsonSerDe | `timestamp.formats` |  | not applied, logged when not empty | ignored |  | Not applied: timestamps are read with DuckDB's default format; a warning is logged. |
| Hive JsonSerDe | `ignore.malformed.json` |  | ignored | ignored |  | Not a property of this SerDe: a malformed line fails the query. |

## Options

| Option | Reader | Writer |
|---|---|---|
| delimiter | read_csv delim | COPY delimiter |
| quote | read_csv quote | COPY quote |
| escape | read_csv escape | COPY escape |
| null_string | read_csv nullstr | COPY nullstr |
| header_lines | read_csv skip | COPY header (at most one line) |
| null_for_invalid_data | TRY_CAST instead of CAST of each field | - |
| false_unless_true | boolean field is lower(field) = 'true' | - |
| ignore_errors | read_json ignore_errors | - |

## Conversions

| Conversion | Meaning |
|---|---|
| byte_code | LazySimpleSerDe byte: a number from -128 to 127 is a byte code ('9' is a tab), else the first character; empty is '\001' |
| character | the first character; empty is the default |
| text | the value as is |
| count | a non-negative integer; empty is 0 |
| boolean | true when the value is 'true' in any case |
